items.t: Why Ukraine’s defense industry may have hit a ceiling
items.m: Ukraine’s defense industry fell apart after the Soviet Union collapsed, and by the start of Russia’s full-scale invasion, the country made almost no weapons of its own. After the invasion, however, the sector grew rapidly, largely thanks to European funding. That growth has let Ukraine keep fighting even as U.S. support has shrunk and the European Union has been unable to supply enough weapons.

items.m: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky claimed seven naval drones carried out two attacks off the coast of Benghazi. The attack on Russian vessels transporting weaponry demonstrates Kyiv's capacity to strike Moscow's interests wherever they might be.

items.t: German military seeks to make use of Kyiv's Delta analysis tool
items.m: BERLIN, Nov 23 - Germany and Ukraine on Monday signed a letter of intent that will eventually enable the Bundeswehr to use Kyiv's battle management system Delta, German Defence Minister Boris Pistorius said.

items.t: Britain says SpaceX restrictions in Ukraine 'dented confidence and trust'
items.m: KYIV, Nov 23 - Britain's defence minister said on Monday that restrictions on the use of SpaceX's satellite communications by Ukraine's military have caused concern among European governments and damaged trust in the company's services.

items.t: NATO to send early-warning system aircraft to Poland after missiles incident
items.m: Three Russian Kh-101 missiles landed in Poland last week, prosecutors said, adding to fears that Russia's war in Ukraine could spill into NATO territory.

items.t: What Russian warship did Ukraine just sink?

items.t: Merz says it was a "mistake" not to admit Ukraine into NATO in 2008
items.m: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz told reporters the Russian invasion of Ukraine would likely not have happened if allies had agreed to admit Kyiv in 2008 during a summit in Bucharest.

items.t: More than 700,000 Russian troops died in the war in Ukraine by late September 2026, Meduza and Mediazona estimate
items.m: On November 1, news broke that hackers from the Belarusian Cyber Partisans and Silent Crow had breached the website of Rosstat, Russia’s federal statistics agency, and obtained data on Russian military losses in the war through fall 2026. The hackers used that data to produce their own estimate of how many Russians had been killed on the front lines. They also shared the database with reporters, including those at Meduza and Mediazona, which have been tracking Russia’s military death toll together for several years. items.t: Blasts and shrapnel account for 92% of recorded Russian military deaths in Ukraine, iStories reports. Gunshot wounds account for less than 2%.
items.m: Explosions and shrapnel accounted for 92% of recorded Russian military deaths in the war against Ukraine. The investigative outlet iStories highlighted the figure after reviewing a database of Russian front-line military losses compiled by Rosstat, Russia’s federal statistics agency, and shared by hackers. Meduza and other news outlets reviewed the same data at the same time.

items.t: What strike on Russian ship in Libya says about spread of Ukraine war
items.m: Ukraine's sinking of a Russian battleship at a port in Libya raises the stakes of the war a notch, writes Frank Gardner.

items.t: Libya's east seeks UN probe into claims Ukrainian military present in west
items.m: Authorities in divided Libya's east called on Monday for the United Nations to investigate claims that Ukrainian forces were present in the country's west, as they lodged a complaint over Ukrainian attacks on two Russian ships off Benghazi. The strikes on Sunday, claimed by Kyiv, come as Ukraine steps up strikes against Russia far from the front lines of their war. FRANCE 24's Emerald Maxwell reports.

items.t: How far will Ukraine war spread? Kyiv targets Russian vessels in Libya
items.m: Talk about spillover. In the Libyan port of Benghazi, Ukraine claiming responsibility for the sinkings first of a Russian warship and then a cargo vessel. That’s on top of the sanctioned ship struck in the Baltic Sea that’s since strayed into Finland’s waters. Legitimate targets?

items.t: Ukraine claims it sank Russian warship off Libya
items.m: Ukraine on Monday claimed it was behind strikes on two Russian vessels off Libya, including one that sank a modern warship, in the latest spillover from Moscow's invasion. The attacks on Sunday near the Libyan port of Benghazi come at a time when Ukraine has stepped up its daring strikes against Russia far from the frontlines in retaliation for Moscow's deadly invasion. FRANCE 24's Gulliver Cragg reports from Kyiv.

items.t: NATO warns of intensifying threats as Ukraine peace proposals face key questions
items.m: Henri Vanhanen, a senior fellow with the Transatlantic Security Initiative, joined Euronews’ new show Europe Tonight to discuss growing security concerns and the prospects for peace in Ukraine.

items.t: Russia warns of 'preventive nuclear attack' as Medvedev claims Ukraine, NATO crossed line
items.m: Dmitry Medvedev claims Ukraine and NATO have crossed thresholds that could make a preventive nuclear attack by Russia possible, warning Kyiv's allies.

items.t: EU moves to ban Russian flags at sports events under new sanctions
items.m: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen has announced a proposal for the next sanctions package over Russia’s war against Ukraine that would ban Russian teams and individual athletes from competing under the Russian flag at events in the EU in the future. The plan also includes banning the display of official Russian symbols and restricting financial flows from Russian sponsors to sports and cultural associations based in Europe. Russian nationals would also no longer be allowed to...

items.t: Tripoli condemns Ukraine strike on Russian ships, seeks explanation
items.m: The Tripoli-based Libyan Foreign Ministry denounced on Monday an Ukrainian attack on two Russian ships near the eastern city of Benghazi, asking for an explanation from Kyiv. The a...

items.t: Legal battle looms over potential Russian return to international sport
items.m: The IOC is pushing for Russia to return to Olympic competition after years of exclusion due to the war in Ukraine but a legal quagmire looms ahead of growing opposition to a potential comeback.

items.t: Zelenskiy says intelligence shows Russia planning new strikes on Ukraine
items.m: Nov 23 - Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said on Monday that intelligence showed Russia planned new strikes on Ukraine, and he urged the United States and other countries to take note as supplies of air defence systems depended on their decisions.

items.m: The GUR, Ukraine's military intelligence agency, said Russian forces began using the K5-K variant of the Geran-5 drone in attacks on Ukrainian cities at the beginning of autumn.

items.t: Russia protests Estonia’s planned land border closure and again accuses it of letting Ukrainian drones use its airspace
items.m: Russia’s Foreign Ministry summoned Estonia’s acting chargé d’affaires in Moscow, Marek Juhtegi, and lodged a “strong protest” over Estonia’s accusation that Moscow tried to set fire to a defense plant and the Estonian government’s decision to close the border with Russia.

items.t: Russia’s statistics agency listed heart disease as the cause of Ukrainian journalist Viktoriia Roshchyna’s death in Russian custody, leaked records show
items.m: Official Russian documents attribute Ukrainian journalist Viktoriia Roshchyna’s death in Russian custody to heart disease and pulmonary edema. BBC News Russian, Verstka, and iStories reported the finding after reviewing leaked data from Rosstat, Russia’s federal statistics agency.

items.t: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz says it was a mistake to leave Ukraine out of NATO in 2008
items.m: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said Ukraine should have been admitted to NATO in 2008. He made the remarks at a joint press conference with NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte, Die Zeit reported.

items.t: How Ukraine destroyed one of Russia's newest warships
items.m: Ukraine says its naval drones sank one of Russia's newest vessels – the corvette Merkury – in a Libyan port. Seven drones were used in the attack, which also hit a cargo ship which President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Russia used to transport weapons. CBC's Briar Stewart explains what we know about the operation.

items.t: 'A war of unmanned machines, AI and total transparency of the battlefield'
items.m: Speaking with FRANCE 24's Sharon Gaffney, Nobel Peace Prize laureate Oleksandra Matviichuk, Director of the Centre for Civil Liberties, says that today's war in Ukraine "is a war of unmanned machines, AI, total transparency of the battlefield, mass drones attacks and long range weapons, and this means we have to rethink how to protect human beings".

items.m: Military video posted by Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy is said to show the country's naval drone attacks on Russian ships near Libya, thousands of miles from the battlefield. Charlie D'Agata reports.

items.t: Hacked Russian data suggests nearly 500,000 soldiers dead, reports say
items.m: Data allegedly stolen by hackers from Russia’s statistics agency Rosstat show the number of recorded Russian military dead is approaching 500,000, several Russian media outlets and German news magazine Der Spiegel reported on Monday. The outlets said they had gained access to the data set, which the hacker groups Cyberpartisans and Silent Crow are said to have taken in an attack on the agency. Reports say the groups are close to the Belarusian opposition or to pro-Ukrainian collectives. Rosstat...

items.t: Russia claims strikes on Starlink terminals, drone sites in Ukraine's Sumy
items.m: Russia's military conducted attacks on military sites in Ukraine's Sumy region using drones and missile strikes. In a separate incident, an overnight attack in Zaporizhzhia resulted in injuries to 11 individuals, including severe cases. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy issued warnings about impending Russian strike preparations while urging increased military aid from allies. He emphasized the importance of anti-ballistic missile systems for Ukraine's defense against aggression.

items.t: Russian attack kills 2 people, wounds 22 in Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia, official says
items.m: Nov 24 - A Russian attack killed 2 people and injured 22 more, including 2 children, in Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia overnight, Ivan Fedorov, co-head of the Zaporizhzhia Regional Defense Council, said on Telegram on Tuesday.
